html:
The 1977 Egyptian bread riots were two days of mass protest across Egypt on 18 and 19 January 1977, after the government cut subsidies on bread, rice, cooking oil and other basics.

President Anwar Sadat had turned from Nasser's state socialism to an "open door" economy. To get loans from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, his government announced the price rises. Within hours, crowds of workers and students filled the streets of Cairo, Alexandria and other cities, attacking police stations, nightclubs and symbols of the new rich.

The army was called out, a curfew was set, and about 80 people were killed and hundreds wounded. The government cancelled the cuts within two days.

The lesson stayed with every Egyptian government after: bread prices are close to untouchable. Egypt's cheap subsidised flatbread, called aish baladi, feeds tens of millions to this day. Sadat blamed communists, and soon after turned toward peace with Israel and closer ties with the United States. Bread prices were again a cry of the Arab Spring in 2011.
sum: The 1977 Egyptian bread riots were two days of mass protest across Egypt on 18 and 19 January 1977, after the government cut subsidies on bread, rice, cooking oil and other basics.
